structured.approach: I followed the data-science-steps procedure for DS-07 and read the three contracted inputs: task.code, task.unit_tests and feat.stories. I tried git status and CI through Bash, but hook G9 blocked both, because DS-07 may run no shell commands and only the spine runs git push and merge. So this step made no commit and no push. Instead I checked the working tree with Read, Glob and Grep: risk.py, __init__.py, the test names and a search for secret patterns. I read the git metadata files (config, HEAD, packed-refs, reflogs) to find the push target and to check for merge conflicts. I checked shared memory for the commit-message convention. Then I wrote task.commit as a commit plan for the spine to run: two commits, each message starting with its story ID, the file lists, the CI result carried from DS-06, the conflict check, the push target and the secrets finding.

claims.text: Commit messages must start with the story ID.
The ap_forecast changes implement two stories: the rule-based vendor_risk level (STORY-03) and the optional risk in build_explanation_request (STORY-04).
DS-05 changed README.md, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py and src/ap_forecast/explain.py, and added docs/ and src/ap_forecast/risk.py. predict.py and models.json are unchanged.
DS-06 added tests/test_risk.py and extended tests/test_forecast.py with test_request_with_risk and test_request_without_risk_unchanged.
The working tree's risk.py has the HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30 and MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 thresholds with strict '>', and __init__.py sets __version__ to 0.10.0 and exports vendor_risk.
The last CI run on this working tree passed: 11 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, coverage 100.0, no static issues.
The coverage gate for the repository is 90%.
The remote origin is https://github.com/arghya05/ap-forecast-sample.git, and HEAD is refs/heads/feature/story.
origin/dev, origin/main, local dev, local feature/story and origin/feature/story all point to commit d67e866, so no merge conflict is expected.
Neither the code nor the tests need a secret in any environment, and no database or Databricks change is involved.
A search of the checkout for api_key, secret, token and password patterns found only the max_tokens config field.
Shell commands, including git commit and push, are blocked for this step and are run only by the spine.
The PR is raised in a later step (DS-09), on the pushed commit.

open_questions: CP-1: The workbook says to push to the central/main repository, but agents may not push to protected main. Is pushing feature/story to origin the intended reading? Interim answer: push feature/story only.
CP-2: Should this be two commits (one per story) or a single commit? Interim answer: two commits; the output also gives a single-commit fallback.
CP-3: The workbook outcome says the PR is being raised, but DS-09 raises the PR. Confirm that no PR is expected from DS-07.
Carried from earlier steps: CQ-C2 (version 0.10.0), CQ-DS-1 (test file split), UT-1 (interim answers PQ-1, TQ-5, TQ-4), CQ-DS-3, RAQ-1, TQ-8, PQ-5.
structured.summary: The STORY-03 and STORY-04 code is ready to commit, but this step did not commit or push it. The hook blocks all shell commands for DS-07, so the spine has to run the commit and the push. I wrote task.commit as the plan for that. It gives two commits on feature/story, one per story, and each message starts with its story ID (STORY-03 or STORY-04) and traces to FEAT-ZD-48600, the task and the acceptance criteria. It lists the files in each commit. It carries the DS-06 CI result: 11 tests passed, coverage 100.0 against the 90% gate, no static issues. That result covers both commits together; the tree after the first commit alone has not been tested. No merge conflict is expected, because all local and origin branches point to d67e866, but the spine should fetch before pushing because I could only read the refs on disk. The push target is origin/feature/story only; main and dev are not touched. No secrets are needed, and none are in the files. DS-09 raises the PR. There are no blocking questions.

tool_input.command: git status --short && git branch -a && git remote -v && git log --oneline -5 && git config user.name; git config user.email; git diff --stat
